This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Vinorelbine, a structurally related vinca alkaloid, has absolute oral bioavailability of 43 ± 14% (close to 40% by AUCinf) in fasted patients and 36–43% with food, all above the 20% threshold.
LCS1269, which shares the carbazole-lactam core with the query, is predicted to have human bioavailability greater than 30% based on intestinal absorption.
Ondansetron, a carbazole-containing drug, has absolute oral bioavailability of 50–65% in fasted volunteers and 40% after rifampin pretreatment, supporting that this scaffold can achieve F ≥ 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability data are available for the query molecule itself.
The LCS1269 record is a predicted HIA-based value rather than a measured absolute bioavailability.
Vinorelbine transfer is analog-based; the query has different substituents that could alter absorption or first-pass metabolism.
No query-specific solubility, permeability, or first-pass clearance data are available.
content.decision_summary: Although the physicochemical prior is low, all transferable evidence from structurally related molecules — vinorelbine (F ≈ 40%), LCS1269 (predicted F > 30%), and ondansetron (F ≈ 50–65%) — supports F ≥ 20%. No affirmative evidence supports F < 20%, so the prediction is high.
